gaps.classification: BLOCKING for comparison use; INFERABLE for F17's glyph metric
gaps.why: F17's M-F17.1 measures a 10%-to-90% luminance transition across a glyph stem to a <=1.5 device px tolerance. Steam re-encodes every upload to chroma-subsampled JPEG, which smears a one-pixel stem transition by about a pixel, so a Steam screenshot cannot measure a reference UI's glyph sharpness at that tolerance. It does not need to: F17-F19 are ABSOLUTE thresholds measured on our own UI, not percentile bands drawn from a population. The reference set serves RI-UIX06's 'PERMITTED REFERENCE SET: RI-VIS02 (modern)' declaration and the blind comparison, for which JPEG is fine.

dead_ends: /workshop/browse/?section=screenshots renders the MOD workshop for any app that has one and returns zero screenshots, indistinguishable from 'no results'. Confirmed by a previous agent's fossil ids.json: Elden Ring only, every other app empty. Use the apphub homecontent endpoint instead.

Steam rate-limits the DETAIL endpoint hard: 8 concurrent fetches of /sharedfiles/filedetails/?id= returned HTTP 429 and a ~27.3 KB 'Steam Community :: Error' page for 960 of 1000 requests -- and that error page is a plausible-sized 200-ish HTML body a naive cache will happily store. 3 workers with 0.7s sleep is safe. The LISTING endpoint is not rate-limited.

HEAD is useless on images.steamusercontent.com: Akamai returns Content-Length: 92 for a sizeable minority of URLs (11 of 48 in one sample) while a plain GET on the identical URL returns the real 701,272-byte JPEG. A HEAD-based liveness check would reject a quarter of a good catalogue. Use a ranged GET and read Content-Range: bytes 0-1023/<total>.

searchText matches the uploader's title and description, NOT the image. Elden Ring 'equipment screen' top hit (?id=3405289538) is a throne-room cutscene, not a menu. Every UI candidate needs eyes on it before cataloguing.
Skyrim SE's top-rated Steam gallery is mod/ENB contaminated and titles do not disclose it (1.9% mention a mod). See G18 for the three defences.

RDR2 and Witcher 3 Steam screenshots are photo-mode-heavy and section 5a bars photo-mode filters, DoF and vignette. Not fatal -- one clean RDR2 night frame (?id=3544436425) is a textbook exterior_lowlight reference -- but photo_mode must be judged per image, never assumed false.

api.github.com unauthenticated returns 403 (rate limit) and there is no gh CLI in this container. Expanding the 29 globbed sksebp-og.github.io URLs must go via raw.githubusercontent.com directory listing or the MCP GitHub tools.
en.uesp.net still 403s (its own bot protection, per AGENT-PROTOCOL). Not attempted.
Steam store trailers cannot serve video/: all are cut montages and V1/V2 both require 'no cuts' explicitly. The movies[] array in appdetails is a dead end for this purpose.
'overcast' is genuinely scarce -- 3 to 8 hits per game against 50 for dramatic queries. Not a search failure to retry; it is a property of what people upload. See G16.

The bare https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/<A>/<B>/ URL is the ORIGINAL; the ?imw=5000&... variant is an Akamai re-encode. Verified twice: bare returned 10,002,569 bytes against a page stating 9.539 MB, and on another file bare 701,272 vs imw=5000 672,633. Codex's choice of the bare URL was correct -- preserve it.
